dataset.description:
1. What data will be collected or produced, and what existing data will be re-used?
1.1 Which existing data you will re-use and under which terms of use.
All data will be originally produced within this project, no previously existing data will be re-used.
1.2 If new data will be produced: describe the data you expect your research will generate and the format and volumes to be collected or produced.
We will obtain GROMACS molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories of simulations involving pharmaceutical drugs and drug-like compounds with lipid bilayers, which will be analyzed to obtain information regarding permeation of the former across the latter.
1.3 How much data storage will your project require in total?
Several hundreds of GB, close to 1 TB.
2 What metadata and documentation will accompany the data?
2.1 Indicate what documentation will accompany the data.
No special documentation is required. MD trajectories will be organized in folders named according to the individual simulated compounds. The folders containing the trajectories will be accompanied by all input files, some of which will contain comments regarding particular simulation or topology choices. Complementary explanations will also be provided in the open-access articles where the research will be published. Users with previous experience in MD simulation with GROMACS will experience no difficulty in interpreting and/or re-using the data.
2.2 Indicate which metadata will be provided to help others identify and discover the data.
The possibility of access to these data will be publicized in the project publications. Inside each folder of data, a short "readme" file will describe the basic system to which the folder concerns, also pointing to the published article for additional details.
3 How will data and metadata be stored and backed up during the research?
3.1 Describe where the data and metadata will be stored and backed up during the project
During the 12 months of duration of the project, trajectories will be stored in the workplace computers of the team members, who will be busy analyzing them. Two identical complete copies of the results will also be stored in independent external hard disk drives.
3.2 How will data security and protection of sensitive data be taken care of during the research?
Not applicable (no sensitive data).
4 How will you handle issues regarding the processing of personal information and intellectual property rights and
ownership?
4.1 Will you process and/or store personal data during your project?
No.
4.2 How will ownership of the data and intellectual property rights to the data be managed?
The data is owned by the team members, who will be the only people with access to the data while it remains unpublished. After publication, access will be granted for consultation and/or re-use to interested academic researchers, for research purposes, with full acknowledgement of the original owners and citation of the relevant original publications.
5 How and when will data be shared and preserved for the long term?
5.1. How will data be selected for long-term preservation?
All data resulting from the project will be preserved for at least 15 years.
5.2 What data will be made available for re-use?
All data resulting from the project will be made available.
5.3 When will the data be available for re-use, and for how long will the data be available?
Data available as soon as article is published.
5.4 In which repository will the data be archived and made available for re-use, and under which license?
The data will be preferably archived in the Zenodo repository, built and operated by CERN and OpenAIRE (https://zenodo.org/) and/or the "Repositório de Dados Científicos" (repository of scientific data, https://dados.rcaap.pt/), which is part of the national network of Portuguese open access scientific repositories (https://www.rcaap.pt/). Additionally, local copies of the data will also be stored in external disk drives kept by the team members. We intend to make the data available for re-use (after publication by the team members of the original research results), under the Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 licence (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0).
5.5 Describe your strategy for publishing the analysis software that will be generated in this project.
At this stage, it is not anticipated that specific tools or software (e.g. specific scripts, codes or algorithms developed during the project) will be required to access, interpret or (re-)use the data. Should any such requirement take place, all scripts/codes/algorithms produced by the team members during the project will be made available together with the data.
6 Data management responsibilities and resources
6.1 Who (for example role, position, and institution) will be responsible for data management?
The PI (Luís M. S. Loura, Associate Professor at the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Coimbra) or, in his absence, the co-PI (Hugo A. L. Filipe, Researcher at the School of Health Sciences, Polytechnic of Guarda).
6.2 What resources (for example financial and time) will be dedicated to data management and ensuring that data will be FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable)?
The team members will take care of uploading the data to the chosen free repository and storing copies in local external hard disk drives. No additional resources will be needed to prepare data for deposit or to cover any charges from data repositories.
Coimbra, 3 October 2024
Luís Miguel Santos Loura
Principal Investigator
